text.p: Italian bonds and Btp futures closed just off session lows, with futures sliding further in Liffe APT trading, dragged down by T-bonds on a raft of U.S. data.
Traders noted that while the thin Italian market fell on Thursday on profit-taking, losses in today's pre-weekend session were entirely due to the slump on the U.S. debt market.

"European bond markets already began showing signs of weakness yesterday but were supported by the U.S. market. But today selling was triggered after stronger than expected U.S. jobs data only to continue after the NAPM index," one said.
